problem: Existing embodied benchmarks evaluate high-level task planning and low-level navigation/manipulation in isolation, rely on PDDL/final-state goal conditions, and LLM conversation data is incompatible with mobile-manipulation trajectory data, so LLMs are poorly grounded.
motivation: Home robots must interleave planning, navigation and manipulation in continuous space and recover from failures. Evaluating only single steps or final states misses flexible solutions and per-module diagnosis, and LLMs need grounding and feedback-driven adaptation to work.
key_idea: Build a unified benchmark (EMMOE) with a 100-task mobile manipulation dataset, keypath-based language metrics (TP, SER, SRR), and an agent (HomieBot) whose Video-LLaVA planner is trained with SFT+DPO on decomposed subtask data and drives lightweight low-level policies with typed error feedback.
insight: Small amounts of LMM-trainable augmented data (3.3k SFT, 9k DPO) substantially reduce grounding errors (F2 object hallucination dominates baseline failures, but is much lower for HomieBot), letting a 7B model rival o1. DPO helps on the train split but hurts generalization on the held-out test split (SR 20.00 -> 16.67, SRR 6.55 -> 3.08), while SER stays stable. Low-level execution is a bottleneck (Pick SR only 22.45%), which the error taxonomy lets one separate from planning errors.
method: EMMOE-100 dataset: 100 Habitat-Lab 2.0 Replica scenes, Fetch robot teleoperated, trajectories decomposed into 966 subtasks (action, target, low-level model choice) with 4 egocentric views, reasoning annotations and deliberate failures with re-plans; five task attributes
Metrics: Task Progress (max keypath match ratio), Success End Rate (successes / trajectories ending with End), Success Re-plan Rate (re-plans in successful runs / all re-plans), plus SR and PLWSR
High-level planner: Video-LLaVA-7B takes 4 directional views, system info, task, inventory, history and feedback, and outputs JSON {analysis, subtask(action,target), model}
Low-level execution: M3 skills with background info; or RT-1-X (pick/place), Octo (open/close), NoMaD (image nav) and PixNav (object nav) without it; each action retried up to 3 times
Error detection: four error types (Logical L1-4, Distance D1-2, Format F1-2, Execution E1-2) checked at several stages and returned as feedback to the planner
SFT augmentation: convert data to conversation format and rewrite task descriptions and analyses 3x with GPT-4o (930 -> 3,720 samples)
DPO augmentation: failed step vs. successful re-plan pairs, plus Order Change, Action Change, Model Change; End only appears as rejected (10,104 pairs)

setting.backbone: Video-LLaVA-7B (SFT then DPO, LoRA) planner + M3 low-level skills (also RT-1-X, Octo, NoMaD, PixNav)
setting.training_data: 90 EMMOE-100 tasks: 3,316 SFT and 8,984 DPO samples (GPT-4o rewritten text augmentation)
setting.observation: four egocentric RGB views (256x256) with textual feedback/inventory/history
setting.action_space: discrete subtasks (Go to, Pick, Place, Open, Close, End) executed by low-level policies in continuous space
setting.privileged: M3 low-level execution setting uses background information (precise target position/state); planner gets no background info

numbers.eval_set_note: all 100 tasks (90 train + 10 test), 3 runs each, max 20 steps
numbers.extra: M3 low-level with background info; planner trained on 90 of the evaluated tasks

numbers.eval_set_note: all 100 tasks, 3 runs each, max 20 steps

results: HomieBot-7B (SFT+DPO) reaches SR 30.30, PLWSR 24.66, TP 51.39 and SER 60.81 on EMMOE-100, beating o1 (SR 28.67, TP 44.52, SER 38.57) and Gemini-1.5-Pro (SR 17.33), though o1 has higher SRR (13.80). On the 10 held-out tasks DPO is worse than SFT except SER, indicating a generalization cost.
limitations: Simulation only (Habitat), with limited actions/space restricting task design; no real-robot evaluation
Only 100 tasks and 10 test tasks, so held-out results are noisy
Standardized output loses information precision, multiple model inferences add time, and low-level policies (esp. Pick, 22.45% SR) bottleneck success
